claims.text: The three core artifacts describe one and the same trip: trip identifier TRP-00530 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, all generated for the 2026-09-18 booking with a consistent pickup timeline (accepted 08:00:40, started 08:06:40, ended 08:40:40). The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on matching identifiers and a matching trip window, so the burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

A route deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01 on the governing trace figure: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 17.08 km against a booked optimal of 13.9 km, an excess of 3.18 km. That excess is 22.88% of optimal_distance_km and so passes the 20% gate, and it is 3.18 km absolute and so passes the 0.8 km gate; both tests pass. The trip_record's rounded 17.1 km convenience copy is not cited for this test, because POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern where the two disagree.

The trace cannot be attacked as gap-ridden or unreliable: it carries 205 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage, zero recorded gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, and its internal distance (17.08 km) matches the trip record's rounded figure. It fails none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so the trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes and the excess stands on the trace alone without any need for independent corroboration.

The driver's 'bus breakdown on the main road' excuse is weightless on this record. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00530-01, is MISSING: its payload is null, its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. With no advisory naming a road or segment and no validity window, POL-RD-03's exoneration comparison cannot be run and is unavailable; the driver's assertion cites no advisory artifact and therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Under POL-RD-13 the excess accordingly stands at the measured figure, the assertion neither reduces it nor supplies an amended optimal, and because the driver has cited no advisory identifier this is a gap in the bundle, not the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction that would force escalation.

No rider-requested detour can be run under POL-RD-04. The chat log for this trip contains 0 messages and is not truncated, so there is no rider instruction, no timestamp and no chat_message.waypoint_hint for the 200 m corroboration test. The clause's test is not merely failed, it is undecidable on the record, and no part of the 3.18 km excess is excluded on this ground.

No relocation adjustment under POL-RD-05 reduces the excess. On the trip record, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no amended endpoints and no re-quote exist; the booked optimal of 13.9 km between Blk 811 Hougang Central and Raffles Place MRT is the correct and only baseline.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on this METERED fare, not discretionary. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.0 surge from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 surcharge + 0 waiting fee - 0 promo = 21.185. charged_total is 26.95, so the refund before rounding is 5.765, rounded UP to SGD 5.80. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below 90% of charged_total, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.80.

The driver's plea that 'the taxi meter is higher than the app's discount cars, that's the tier' is not a route defence. The fare model on this trip is METERED under rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI, and POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare arithmetically against the optimal route; a comparison between product tiers or against an unstated discount-car benchmark has no place in that computation and does not excuse a measured 3.18 km excess.

There is no pass-through liability to net off, and equally none to add on top. The fare breakdown carries no ERP lines at all (off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route totals both 0.00) and no airport surcharge; the refund figure is therefore the POL-RD-02 distance-and-time figure standing alone, and under POL-RD-09 limb (1) no off-route ERP may be added to it on top.

The pooled-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply and cannot be used to inflate the baseline: this trip's vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, so the booked optimal_distance_km of 13.9 km is the ordinary single-rider platform optimal and the measured excess is not attributable to collecting or setting down any co-rider.

claims.text: The POL-RD-01 gates are cleared only marginally and the MATERIAL gate is not cleared at all. Measured on the governing trace figure (gps_trace.trace_distance_km 17.08, against the booked optimal 13.9), the excess is 3.18 km and 22.88% — above the 0.8 km and 20% establishment gates, but far below the 8.0 km and 50% thresholds that make a deviation MATERIAL and engage the driver-profile check in POL-RD-06. This is the marginal end of the range the clause contemplates, and no materiality finding, no POL-RD-06 uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) referral are available on this record.

The driver's trailing profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither test in POL-RD-06 is met: the flag count is below 3 and the ratio is 0.00, below 0.05, with the 40-trip floor comfortably cleared. POL-RD-06(b) therefore cannot uplift any refund to FULL_REFUND and POL-RD-06(c) cannot add a driver-conduct referral. POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting any other profile field — rating, account age, lifetime trips, or the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter, which is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause names — for this test.

There is nothing on the ledger for POL-RD-09 to correct. The fare_breakdown shows tolls_erp 0.00, an empty erp_gantries list, optimal_route_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00 (this trip neither originates nor terminates at an airport, so no surcharge line is even properly chargeable), waiting_time_fee 0.00 and promo_discount 0.00. No off-route ERP refund, no standalone surcharge correction and no billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4) is available to the rider, and limb (1) forbids counting any pass-through line twice on top of the distance-and-time figure.

The only remedy this policy provides is arithmetic, and it is small. POL-RD-02 fixes the ceiling at charged_total less a recomputed fare: charged_total is 26.95; recomputed_fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 22.0) x the 1.0 surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 21.185; the refund is 5.765, rounded UP to 5.80. That is 21.4% of charged_total — below the 90% share that would trigger FULL_REFUND and well above the 0.50 de minimis floor — so the most the rider can recover on a PARTIAL_REFUND, which under POL-GEN-03 returns only 'part of the contested amount', is 5.80, not the 26.95 she contests.

The rider's pleaded grievance is a price-tier comparison, not a measured route loss. Her claim sets 'around fifty dollars' against 'seventy-six', while this trip actually charged 26.95 on a METERED rate card; the gap between a metered taxi meter and an app-quoted car is not a route-deviation loss, and POL-RD-02 supplies no discretion to translate that gap into a refund. The remedy is the recomputation above — arithmetic, not discretionary — and it is capped at 5.80.

Concession, on the driver's behalf: the driver's explanation — a bus breakdown on the main road, so he went via Balestier — cannot be run as an exoneration on this record. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching it; the bundle holds only EV-ADVIS-00530-01, which is MISSING (admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no fact and its absence is citable but proves nothing about traffic). Under POL-RD-13 an uncited traffic assertion is tested against the trip's advisory and nothing else; there being no advisory on file, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and it neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies a closure-adjusted optimal route. The driver therefore does not ask for a finding that the route was justified, and the case falls to be decided on this trip's own numbers.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties, in plain language: this is the route-deviation dispute for trip TRP-00530 (18 Sep 2026, Blk 811 Hougang Central to Raffles Place MRT), and the rider is owed SGD 5.80 of the SGD 26.95 charged.

DISTANCE TEST (POL-RD-01). The governing figure is the trace, not the trip record's rounded copy. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 17.08 km against the booked optimal of 13.9 km on the trip record — an excess of 3.18 km, which is 22.88% of optimal. That clears both establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. It does not clear the materiality gates (more than 8.0 km or more than 50%). No materiality finding therefore arises, and no POL-RD-06 driver-profile uplift or conduct referral is available on this trip.

DRIVER PROFILE (POL-RD-06). Independently, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat pattern is established either way. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral.

TRACE INTEGRITY (POL-RD-07). The trace is not impaired: 205 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. No independent corroboration is required for the excess.

DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE (POL-RD-03 / POL-RD-08 / POL-RD-13). The driver says a bus breakdown on the main road forced the route via Balestier. No traffic advisory covering this trip window is on file: the only one in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00530-01, is MISSING, with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Under POL-RD-13 a traffic assertion is tested against the trip's advisory and nothing else; with no advisory there is nothing to test, POL-RD-03 cannot run, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies a closure-adjusted optimal route. Because the driver's assertion cites no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle, not the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, and it does not escalate the case. The assertion is discarded.

DRIVER'S TIER ARGUMENT. The plea that a metered taxi meter is a higher tier than an app-quoted car is not a route defence. This fare is METERED (rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI) and POL-RD-02 recomputes it arithmetically against the optimal route; a product-tier comparison has no place in that computation and no room is given for it.

REFUND ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02). recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 airport surcharge + 0 waiting fee - 0 promo = 21.185. charged_total is 26.95, so the refund is 26.95 - 21.185 = 5.765, rounded UP to SGD 5.80. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and 21.4% of charged_total, well below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund. The correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.80.

PASS-THROUGH LINES (POL-RD-09). The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and no airport surcharge, so there is nothing to correct as a pass-through and nothing to add on top of the distance-and-time figure.

OTHER CLAUSES CONSIDERED AND FOUND INAPPLICABLE. POL-RD-04 rider-requested detour: the chat log for this trip has 0 messages and no waypoint_hint, so there is no rider instruction to test. POL-RD-05 relocation: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so the booked optimal of 13.9 km stands. POL-RD-12 pooling: vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, so the ordinary single-rider optimal applies and no co-rider collection distance is involved.

ON THE RIDER'S WIDER WORRY. The question of how many other trips went unchecked is not before this tribunal; this ruling decides this trip only. If the rider believes other trips were overcharged, each must be filed on its own record.

Confidence is 0.90. Every artifact this ruling rests on — the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing caps confidence below that and the ruling is comfortably above the 0.70 escalation floor.

To the rider and the driver: the trip TRP-00530 from Blk 811 Hougang Central to Raffles Place MRT was charged SGD 26.95 on a METERED rate card, and a route deviation is established on this trip's own trace. Both advocates' figures agree, and I adopt them.

The deviation (POL-RD-01). The governing figure is the trace, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 17.08 km (the trip record's 17.1 km is a rounded copy and may not be cited for the test). Against the booked optimal of 13.9 km that is an excess of 3.18 km, or 22.88% of optimal. Both establishment gates pass: 3.18 km > 0.8 km and 22.88% > 20%. The deviation is NOT material — 3.18 km is well under 8.0 km and 22.88% is well under 50% — so no driver-profile check under POL-RD-06 is engaged, and no conduct referral follows.

The trace is clean (POL-RD-07). It carries 205 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. It fails none of limbs (a)–(c), so it is not impaired and the excess stands on the trace without independent corroboration.

The driver's explanation (POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08, POL-RD-13). The driver says a bus breakdown on the main road forced the Balestier route. That assertion is tested against the trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00530-01, is MISSING (status MISSING, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0); it names no road, carries no validity window, and can carry no fact. POL-RD-03's comparison therefore cannot be run, the excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and it neither reduces the 3.18 km excess nor supplies a closure-adjusted optimal. Both advocates conceded this, and I record the assertion as discarded. Because the driver cited no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle and not the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, so the case is decided on the numbers rather than escalated (POL-RD-13).

No other adjustment applies. The chat log holds 0 messages, so no rider-requested detour can be run under POL-RD-04. Pickup and dropoff were not amended and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 gives nothing. Vehicle type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, so the pooled baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply and 13.9 km is the ordinary single-rider optimal.

The refund (POL-RD-02). With no exculpatory clause operating, the refund is arithmetic: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 13.9 + 0.28 × 22.0) × the 1.0 surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 surcharge + 0 waiting fee − 0 promo = 21.185. Charged_total is 26.95, so the refund before rounding is 5.765, rounded UP to SGD 5.80. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% share that would trigger FULL_REFUND, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.80.

On the rider's pleaded grievance: the claim sets 'around fifty dollars' against 'seventy-six', but the actual charge here was 26.95 and the gap between a metered taxi tier and an app-quoted car is not a route-deviation loss. POL-RD-02 supplies no discretion to convert that comparison into a refund, so the remedy is the arithmetic figure above.

Pass-through lines (POL-RD-09). The ledger shows no ERP gantries, tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00 and waiting_time_fee 0.00. There is nothing to correct, nothing to add on top, and no billing-integrity referral.

Referrals. None is produced. POL-RD-06(c) does not fire because the deviation is not material and the driver profile shows no pattern (deviation_flags_90d = 0 on 250 completed trips in 90 days). POL-RD-09(4) does not fire because there is no unmatched or phantom charge line.

Confidence. The deciding facts rest on the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown, all at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and this ruling sits well above the 0.70 floor.
